outlook: Grains closed lower Wednesday, giving back part of Tuesday's rally. Wheat led the decline: December Chicago wheat fell nearly 18 cents to $6.87 and Minneapolis December spring wheat lost 9.5 cents to $7.10, even with reports of drone strikes on ships in the Black Sea and U.S. winter wheat planting running behind (36% vs. 46% average). December corn slipped 6 cents to $5.02 and November soybeans dipped 5.5 cents to $12.98, while ICE canola dropped C$15.50; harvest is still behind normal after heavy Midwest rain and traders are positioning ahead of Friday's USDA WASDE and Crop Production reports. Minneapolis cash bids shown are from Tuesday's USDA report, the latest available.
